headline: Give your Claude Code a checkup
summary: Quiet Sunday. One Claude Code self-check trick, one new Gemini money feature, and one vibe coding faceplant.

items.title: Have Claude audit your own setup
items.pitch: Peter Yang recommends two commands that get Fable 5.2 to check your Claude Code setup and suggest changes.
why: After a new model drops, your old prompts and skills may not fit anymore
It reviews your CLAUDE.md, skills, and commands, then suggests fixes
Takes a few minutes and you don't have to change any code
actions: Run /doctor prompt-audit in Claude Code and see what changes it suggests
Then run /claude-api prompt-audit [skill name] on the skill you use most
deep_dive: This is a self-check command inside Claude Code, not a new product. The more rule files you have, the more it's worth running.
Heads up: it only suggests changes, so look them over before applying and don't just accept everything.
items.signals: Peter Yang's tweet has 440 likes · He also wishes Claude Code would prompt you to run it after every new model release

items.title: Lovable apps leaked passports and DMs
items.pitch: An app built with Lovable was reported to expose passport info and over 200,000 private messages. Worth checking whatever you've vibe coded too.
why: Nearly 900 points on HN today, with lots of discussion
With apps made by AI in one click, nobody often checks the permission settings
If your little tools hold sensitive stuff like salary data, the same risk applies
actions: Go back and check the little tools you've built: do they hold sensitive data, and who can open them
Ask Claude Code to go over the access permissions for you
deep_dive: All I have is the headline and the HN numbers. I haven't seen the details of the actual vulnerability, so don't jump to conclusions yet.
Lovable is a platform that builds web apps from a chat. The lesson: an app that got generated isn't necessarily a safe app.

items.title: Gemini can connect to Google Wallet to see your spending
items.pitch: The Gemini app can now read your Google Wallet, build spending charts, and catch subscriptions that quietly raised their prices.
why: A personal finance feature that non-developers can use right away
For now it's only open to Gemini app users in the US
items.signals: Josh Woodward's tweet has 462 likes · Rolling out to US users first
